title: Arrecho
desc: One word, two opposite meanings, and only the tone to go on
setting: Marcos said the word twice in five minutes and meant something different each time.

options.feedback: Ask straight out. Everybody has to have this explained once, and the answer is that the tone decides.
You guessed right from his face. Guessing works until the day it does not.

options.es: ¿Y por qué está enojado el carro?
options.en: And why is the car angry?
options.feedback: A joke that only works if you already know the word. Right now it just looks like you have lost the thread.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: No, hombre. Ahí quiere decir que está bueno. Depende del tono.
steps.en: No, man. There it means it is great. It depends on the tone.

options.es: Siempre depende del tono en este país.
options.en: It always depends on the tone in this country.
options.feedback: You have noticed the pattern behind the word, which is the actual lesson. Half of Nicaraguan Spanish is carried by how it is said.
Understood. He gave you a rule that covers dozens of other words and you took it as one fact.
It is, and saying so ends the explanation early. He was about to give you the other half.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: Pero si yo te digo estoy arrecho con vos, ahí sí cuidado.
steps.en: But if I say to you I am arrecho with you, then watch out.

options.es: Entonces con alguien es enojo. Sin nadie es bueno.
options.en: So with somebody it is anger. With nobody it is good.
options.feedback: You worked out the rule from two examples and said it back. Estar arrecho con alguien is the version nobody says lightly.

options.en: I see, with you it is worse.
options.feedback: Half of it. The half you have is the half that will get you in trouble.
Everybody does, and saying you do not is the kind of claim that gets tested at a table like this.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: Ya la sabés, pues. Usala, pero con cuidado.
steps.en: You have got it now. Use it, but carefully.

options.es: Va pues. Ese carro sí está arrecho.
options.en: Right then. That car really is arrecho.
options.feedback: Straight into the good meaning, on something harmless. That is exactly how you try out a word with two edges.
Say one now, while he is here to tell you if the tone was wrong.

options.en: Better if I do not use it.
options.feedback: It is one of the most Nicaraguan words there is. Leaving it on the shelf keeps you sounding foreign.
